items.title: ⚠️ Model & Semantic Guardrails (e.g., NeMo)

items.title: ⏱️ Traditional OS-Level Sandboxes (e.g., eBPF)

items.title: 🔍 Web3 / DID Network-layer Identity
items.desc: Stays at the 'Network/Chain Layer'. Chain transactions or DID resolutions take hundreds of milliseconds to seconds, failing high-frequency Agent requirements, and cannot enforce local binary runtime boundaries.

benchmarks.title: 3. RCU Concurrent Chaos Benchmarks
benchmarks.desc: Under extreme concurrent chaos (50 threads calling tools while performing high-frequency lock-free RCU swaps), DROS recorded outstanding physical performance in laboratory stress environments:

reality.title: 4. Hardware Limits & Boundaries (DROS Engineering Reality)
reality.desc: As strict system engineers, we make no 'perfectly flawless' marketing promises. We transparently disclose the following physical limits and execution envelopes on real hardware:

points.title: 1. Instruction Cache Jitter
points.desc: Due to CPU instruction L1/L2 prefetching and locality warmth variances, core latency may jitter between 400ns and 900ns. This represents natural hardware behavior rather than a failure of O(1) bitmap complexity.

points.title: 2. Cross-Language FFI / JNI Overhead
points.desc: While DROS's core bitwise logic evaluates in 484.8 ns, transitioning across FFI/JNI boundaries (Python/Go/Java) to invoke the compiled C-ABI library adds a 10μs to 50μs marshaling overhead. This is negligible compared to model inference but should be considered in ultra-high-frequency loops.

points.title: 3. Asynchronous I/O Audit Decoupling
points.desc: To preserve a 484.8ns critical path, DROS decouples file system persistence from FFI execution blocks. We employ lock-free circular ring-buffers for log aggregation, keeping disk writes entirely off the critical security path.

points.title: 4. Double-Buffered RCU Memory Overhead
points.desc: To ensure lock-free concurrent safety during hot-reloads, DROS briefly retains both old and new policy pointers, causing minor memory inflation. Under chaos stress, overall memory usage remains extremely low between 2MB and 5MB.

threat.title: Existential Threat: The Traceless Agent Swarms
threat.desc1: Granting AI models the authority to initiate System Calls is opening a physical gate to malicious execution. A rogue Agent can register domains, compile viruses, and migrate across servers without leaving any human footprints. In terms of forensics and legal liability, this is a catastrophe.
threat.desc2: DROS, acting as the **Root Certificate Authority (Root CA)** for the Agentic Web, forces a non-repudiable cryptographic seal onto every execution. We compile security contracts into a signed `policy.bin` (containing Header, Ed25519 signature, sorted agent/tool index tables, and O(1) capability bitmap matrix). The Agent can reason freely, but the moment it attempts to invoke an unauthorized tool, the DROS microkernel triggers a fail-closed thread panic in 484.8 ns, ending the era of AI blame-shifting.
